posts.cooked:
First time poster here, apologies if I’m in the wrong place here

So I just played a 3 hero solo game, and I came across a combo which seems a bit overpowered. I thought I’d bring it up to see if I’d messed up a rule, or if everyone already knows, or whatever.

I was playing Fanatic, Tachyon and The Visionary, and the Tombs of Anubis, against the Ennead. It had been so simple at first… I was lucky enough to almost defeat the 3 starting Villains with no more coming out… But before I could finish the job, another got pulled. And another. In a couple of turns, Tachyon and Visionary both got toasted, with Fanatic low on health. I almost gave up, but…

Fanatic has the Aegis, 2 copies. As long as you’re wearing one, you can’t die; you lose the Aegis and get a health boost instead. She also has a card (I forget the name) which does obscene damage when she’s low on health… The worse she hurts, the more it hits for. And when Tachyon is down, each turn she can either let someone pull a trashed card back into their hand, or let them draw an extra card.

This gives crazy synergy. When the Aegis drops, you play the other if you have it, and have Tachyon pull the discarded copy back in your hand. Otherwise, draw cards until you can play the damage card for 20-29 damage, then have Tachyon pull that into your hand until the next opportunity arises, playing other cards here and there where useful (especially ones that let you draw more). Presto, you’re almost invincible and dropping huge damage every few turns. Most of the remaining villains got one-shotted. Visionary kept the worst of the environment cards at bay, thankfully.

It has flaws, especially against Ennead. The constant card discarding means that, if you time things wrong, your discard pile can dissappear and take your nuke or armour with it. End Of Days usually helped when it came up due to Set… The only equipment needed is the Aegis, and that isn’t affected by EOD. The main pain was when cards came up that discarded equipment and would affect the Aegis, which is why I kept the copy in-hand as often as possible once I found it. Obviously there was still luck involved… Enough damage in a turn would be enough to get rid of Aegis and go on to finish Fanatic… But mostly it was just a matter of time once I got in this situation.

With this in mind, it actually seems viable to go for a self-destructive Tachyon with other characters there to stop Fanatic from pulling too much damage once she drops to the health levels she wants, or to help her draw more cards to power the big attack. Tachyon can do big hits herself of course, but only after cycling through most of her deck. A downed Tachyon, and enough support or luck, can let Fanatic do the same thing every turn until she needs to put on Aegis or draw more cards.

So… I’m missing something. I have to be, right? Because it seems a bit crazy that a two-character combo (based around one of them being defeated) could lead to pseudo-permanent almost-invulnerability and huge, repeating damage outputs with minor equipment needed.

Totally legit. Wrathful Retribution is always a great choice to fish back out of the trash. Keep in mind though that you need 3 cards to discard each time you play Retribution. Edit: just double checked, you must discard exactly 3 cards for Retribution to deal its damage.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Haha that's very cool :D. I like when you can cycle some kind of cool card into your trash and back over and over again. I can remember one game where I was the Scholar (can't rememberwho we were fighting, or where) and I played DDA* because I like the randomness. Then I think during my Draw phase for that turn I drew my other copy of DDA. So next round, I used it to get the first copy back out of my trash again, so I got it back in-hand in my Draw phase. And repeat for the rest of the game, letting the other two heroes basically play a whole bunch of free cards (obviously not always a good idea but in this case there weren't really any "I don't really want that card to come up" cards). I think one of the other two heroes was TLT, which meant I continued to get extra draw anyway and built up a nice big hand. I intended to go into some Elemental forms if things started getting nasty, but we were never in any real danger from whomever it was we were fighting so I just chained DDA for every round except the final one, in which I think I Turned Loose on the villain or something (with my lovely big hand I'd been building all game thanks to TLT) and nuked him/her to bits. Something's telling me we may have been fighting the Ennead (I have an image of Set being the last villain standing) but I really can't remember now. It was good fun anyway :D.

 

 

 

*In case you're not too familiar with this one, being new to the game, DDA is Don't Dismiss Anything, a one-shot which lets each player choose to either put a card from their trash to the top of their deck, or put the top card of their deck into play.

Mr. Fixer's, take an equipment card from trash and put it directly in play. Allowing Fanatic to never have to spend her play phase on Aegis and Tachyon won't have to retrieve it!

But for incap-power cheese, it's hard to top Horus of Two Horizons Ra.  Against any villain who doesn't play extra cards, and has at least one relatively harmless card in his deck, he can guarantee that villain never gets any further into their deck after Ra drops.  Imagine The Chairman forced to constantly replay an Enforcer over and over and over again.  (You'd have to kill the Operative first, but that was probably your plan anyway; at least it would mean there could never be a prison break, which is huge enough.)  Not so great against Spite, Omnitron, or of course the Vengeance Five, but a lot of villains will just insta-lose to that incap ability.

posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked:
I just confidently took on Advanced Mad Bomber Blade in Rook City.  I wouldn't call it a steamroll, but Blade clearly thrives on being underestimated.  I knew I should probably have had AZ play defensively as I usually do, but I was in a hurry to get rid of the ever-deadlier Mad Bomber and get onto the I-thought-pretty-harmless Death Ray side, so I had AZ burn his health like Ronway usually does, dealing lots of damage with Isothermic Transducer whenever the bombs went off around him.  Meanwhile, O-X largely avoided Components and just had Elemental Plating + RPS.  Alone of the heroes, Naturalist played defensively, with Resilient Hide doing a lovely job of protecting him; Unity just wasn't having great luck.  The Environment put some DR on the Baron, then a Racketeer shot us a little, and Natch went into Gazelle so this wouldn't happen again.  Unity popped a Pylon to make Bee Bot and Platform Bot, neither of which would survive for a moment against the 7-damage Bomb that was coming - so since none of the other heroes had Enviro destruction (O-X Timeshifted out a Bio-Engineering Beam just after this), Unity ordered one of her new Bots to kill the other one, so that in dying it would take out the Twisting Back Alleys and leave the Baron fully vulnerable again.

So the Baron explodes for the third time, and after the dust settles, he himself has just 2 HP left, while Unity is at 5 and AZ at 6, with OX also in single digits and Natch at about 12.  Then the Baron plays his card for the turn - Hasten Doom, followed by Devious Disruption.  Unity goes down no matter what, and I decide that AZ with all his equipment gone and 1 HP left isn't worth much, so I kill him too (he dies in pretty much half of my games, despite my usually playing him defensively, but this is the first time I recall having allowed him to die on purpose, when it wasn't a matter of a hit going to some almost-dead hero and him being the least useful).  But OX seems like he still has a chance, so I let him keep the Plating+RPS combo, enabling him to instantly kill the Mad Bomber.  I had not read ahead to refresh my memory exactly how the promo works, not realizing that O-X was going to lose his stuff anyway, and that Advanced games are a really bad place to kill Alpha Blade in the middle of his own turn.  Blade whips out his Death Ray and immediately charges it with the souls of a fallen Blade Battalion.  A round later, Scum and Villainy into a couple of Hasten Dooms has finished off O-X and left Natch at just 2 HP (and, just to be insulting, Blade has healed the 9 damage Natch managed to deal while briefly being a Crocodile); he turtles up with a full round of Rhino action, giving him DR 3 so that he entirely shrugs off the Scum & Villainy damage, but the Death Ray charge is 7 damage and there's a Blighted Streets on top of that.

I can't really complain; I asked for it, and the game wasn't a complete shut-out...I did deal about 50 damage even through light reduction, and did decent amounts of healing and armoring.  Without those Devious Disruptions, I'd probably have won.  But I am definitely done taking the Mad Bomber for granted; I never thought a guy whose entire turn consists of "do a little damage, trash my top card, trash my top card, go" could be dangerous, yet he manages.

I know some heroes have very strong incap powers but I never bother looking at them.  Why? well because mostly my group doesn't like to let people die and we put a strong priority on keeping people alive through the whole game.  When we win, 90% of the time that means no incapped heros.  On the other 10% heroes get incapped with only a round or two left.

This is strictly a preference of play for us, I know some heroes are really good incapped, but we don't like it thematically and hate it from a play stand point.  To be more specific I like that they game incapped players something to do rather than being out of the game, its just that everyone in my group finds it much much much less fun than having a full hero going on.

Put these two reasons together and we have a thematic and a maximize fun reason to try out best to never let anyone get incapped, even if it would actually benefit the team.  And we do pretty well at it.

posts.cooked: Yeah, I've almost never intentionally incapped a hero no matter how useful their ability would be, even though I'm playing solitaire.  My Spite game last night, I went to great effort keeping all heroes alive rather than just going for the throat; it took much longer, but I got a lot of satisfaction from keeping Expatriette from dying yet again.  I think I've only once or twice intentionally killed a hero when they were utterly hamstrung and couldn't accomplish anything with a normal turn, and only toward the end of a game.  (But of course, I've never played Horus of Two Horizons Ra....)
